phase.title: Rates are rising, so money is moving to cash
points: Gold, silver, crypto and tech shares are all falling together. That usually means one thing is driving everything: borrowing is getting dearer.
The Reserve Bank lifted the cash rate to 4.85% in November. Inflation is 3.9% and forecast to stay above 3% until the end of 2027, pushed up by energy prices.
Term deposits and bonds now pay a solid return with little risk, so things that pay no income (gold, silver, crypto) and high-priced tech shares lose their appeal.
Australian shares are holding up better than US tech: the ASX 200 is close to its high for the year while the Nasdaq has slipped since early October.
Gold and silver peaked in late January and have been falling since. Silver has more than halved from that peak.
phase.housing: Home values are falling. Nationally they dropped 1.2% in October, the seventh monthly fall in a row, and nearly every Adelaide suburb is down over three months. Higher rates have cut what a typical household can borrow by about $71,000 since February.
phase.watch: Falling fuel prices and a pause from the Reserve Bank would be the first signs of a turn. In past cycles bonds recover first, then gold, then shares, and housing last, usually 6 to 12 months after rates stop rising.
